core_obligations: Uniqueness (proof lines 1981-1996): assuming that a preadditive structure exists for which the localization functor is additive, the displayed chain of equalities forces s^{-1}f + s^{-1}g = s^{-1}(f + g), so the structure is unique if it exists, and the author correspondingly defines the sum of two classes to be the class of s^{-1}(f + g).

Well-definedness of the addition (proof lines 1998-2037): for a second representation of the same two morphisms with denominator s', a common refinement s_3 together with a_1 and a_2 is produced, and the author checks that s_3^{-1}(a_1(f + g)) = s_3^{-1}(a_2(f' + g')), so the sum does not depend on the chosen representatives.

Bilinearity in the second variable (proof lines 2039-2066): given gamma represented as t^{-1}h, the morphisms a and t' supplied by LMS2 and the displayed commutative diagram give gamma composed with (alpha + beta) equal to (gamma alpha) + (gamma beta).

Bilinearity in the first variable (proof lines 2068-2079): given delta represented as r^{-1}i, filteredness of the category of morphisms with fixed target produces a common denominator s' and maps a'' and b'' with the required commutativity, after which (alpha + beta) composed with delta is computed to equal (alpha delta) + (beta delta).
proof_roadmap: Read off uniqueness from additivity of the localization functor and define the sum accordingly.
Prove that the definition is independent of the representatives using a common refinement.
Check bilinearity of the composition in both variables.
Conclude that the functor is additive.
difficulty_reason: The lemma produces a preadditive structure on a localization of a preadditive category at a left or right multiplicative system, uniquely determined by asking the localization functor to be additive (statement lines 1970-1977). The proof is a complete argument for the left case: the structure is first forced by additivity (proof lines 1981-1996), the proposed sum is shown to be well defined by refining two representations to a common denominator (proof lines 1998-2037), and the two bilinearity checks are carried out with the morphisms supplied by the multiplicative system axioms and the filteredness of the relevant category (proof lines 2039-2079). The non-formal content is the two refinement arguments. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
